notes.title: Factions and upcoming Demo update
notes.notes: [p]Hey people,[/p][p][/p][p]Alex 13 here.[/p][p][/p][h1]Demo update[/h1][p]First of all - the Demo will be updated next Friday. Expect more polish and QoL features, a bunch of new enemy types, and a Faction system.[/p][p][/p][h1]Factions[/h1][p]All enemies in ToP are divided into Factions like Outlaws, Hordes, Undead etc. [/p][p]When the Dungeon is generated, the game now determines which Faction will primarily inhabit it. No more mixed salad of Orc Warlords (Hordes), Wizards (Outlaws) and Rats (Monsters). There will now be consistency with some randomness - so if it's an Undead-inhabited dungeon, expect lots of Undead with occasional representatives of other factions. [/p][p][/p][p]Faction enemies differ in their typical resistances - Undead, for example, have high resistance to Dark damage but no resistance at all to Light damage.[/p][p][/p][p]Since the game will now show the type of dungeon inhabitants, it's another decision making layer for you, adventurers. Is your party Dar magic heavy? Don't go fight undead! Full of Paladins and Clerics? Yes, you will crush them![/p][p][/p][h1]Other stuff[/h1][p]The last map is coming into shape pretty well - and it's my favorite in terms of atmosphere. I love dark crypts, you know.[/p][p]A bunch of new high-level spells are implemented, so more tools to play with in the full game. [/p]

notes.notes: [p]Hey people,[/p][p][/p][p]Alex 13 here.[/p][p][/p][p]We've made 2 major improvements to the game:[/p][olist][*][p]Added several new enemy types and summons.[/p][/*][*][p]Implemented a Lore Collection mechanic[/p][/*][/olist][h1]New Creatures[/h1][p]For time so long the game had only 9 enemy types and no summons, despite mechanics to support them were ready.[/p][p]We've finally found capacity to work on new Creatures. Implemented all [b]summons[/b] and [b]5 new enemy types[/b] - more to come![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/ee8c1ca679ccdfde9c5f7370f88e96362f30c17c.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/327ca0a69376f3f5a50adc2025d7bd3800a18235.png"][/img][/p][h1][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/394c5ec0b30bf7fb5d1b8ce8d0a628298baece49.png"][/img][/h1][h1]Lore Collection[/h1][p]It's quite simple, but we feel empowers engagement. There are 30 lore pieces you can find, describing the world you're adventuring in. [/p][p][/p][p]Some of the texts are quite eye-opening - thus, they are locked as set rewards. Collect 5 Lore Texts of a Set to unlock and claim the 6th Set Lore Text, and a resource reward. [/p][p]These crown jewels answer the most important lore questions and will allow you to understand that [b]\[REDACTED][/b].[/p][p][/p][h1]Next steps[/h1][p]We'll be focusing on Spells for the next sprint (2 weeks) - with intention to finalize all Magic Schools spells so all 90 of them are ready and playable.[/p][p][/p][p]Thanks.[/p][p][/p][p]Alex 13, out.[/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: The feature I'm personally in love with
notes.notes: [p]Hey people,[/p][p][/p][p]Alex 13 here, with GREAT news![/p][p][/p][p]I'm a type of player who LOVES tinkering with my builds in games. If the game provides enough depth to allow me to think, create, test, and iterate on builds - that's the game right up my valley. [/p][p]Even more so if the game allows me to multiclass or create custom classes. A good example of this approach is astounding [url="https://store.steampowered.com/app/259680/Tales_of_MajEyal/"]Tales of Maj'Eyal[/url] by Darkgod - one of my favorite games, period. After I spent hundreds of hours there playing preset classes, I spend another several hundreds of hours playing my custom classes. They break the balance, yes, but in a sooooo fun way![/p][p][/p][p]While Titans of the Past provides a respectable number of 35 playable classes to experiment with - each with a set of Skills, a unique Class skills, and interesting Class Abilities, and each class either goes into one of the 4 character archetypes (Fighter, Cleric, Mage, Rogue) or blends two or more of them, it wasn't enough. Personally for me, as a player. And as a team we're making a game that drives us crazy in a good way. [strike]And as a leader of the team I can force my people to make what I want.[/strike][/p][p][/p][p]So we thought about what can we do to drastically increase the depth of the game's roleplay system and build-crafting potential. And come up with a Custom Class Constructor (CCC).[/p][h1]Custom Class Constructor[/h1][p]Basically, CCC is an [b]ability to create your own custom class[/b] by cherry-picking the [b]Skills[/b] a character with this class will have, and defining their [b]maximum Masteries[/b]. With a point-buy system, because it's the most logical way of doing this, and also because point-buy system is DND-ish enough to support the tabletop game feel of Titans of the Past.[/p][p][/p][p]This already allows you to create and roleplay a huge part of what fantasy characters could be imagined. You can make a swordmaster with Grandmaster in Sword, Two-Handed, True Melee, and Arms Mastery. Give him Expert in Light Armor and you're good to go. Or an Elemental Lord with GMs in all elemental spell schools. Or utilitarian Bard with Disarm Traps and Perception + his auras.[/p][p][/p][p]But this still wasn't enough. Because you already saw all these common Skills and played with the characters that utilize them. The most unique and interesting Skills in the game are Class Skills. They provide you fancy stull like casting a Lightning Bolt with a melee attack, or make your melee attacks AOE, or give you a chance to make a second melee/ranged attack for free and instantly, or heal a random ally when you do something, etc. etc. etc. The possibilities are quite endless here. [/p][p][/p][p]However, the limitation here is that each Class has its own Class Skill and that's it. It's good for making classes distinctive and for balancing the game. Meanwhile the CCC is meant to be a reward for the most consistent players who have beaten the game's last difficulty. So we see no reasons to not provide such players with a complete toolset to break the game however they like.[/p][p][/p][p]So:[/p][list][*][p]CCC is a reward for beating the game's last difficulty.[/p][/*][*][p]CCC allows you to pick for your Custom Classes EVERY skill in the game - [b]including Class Skills[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Thus you can 'multiclass' - create spellswords, necromantic clerics, arcane archers, supercharged melee/ranged/caster fighters. [/p][/*][*][p]The possibilities are endless, and Class Skills provide fun and engaging mechanics combinations not available to preset classes.[/p][/*][*][p]Feel free to make the most imbalanced and crazy-powerful party you can imagine.[/p][/*][*][p]But only after 'winning' the game.[/p][/*][/list][p]You still can't just grab every skill and set it to Grandmaster - the point-buy system won't allow you. So if you want something cohesive, powerful, and interesting - you have to think. I've already spent more than 30 hours just theorycrafting builds for our game - and let me tell you that's one of the best feelings a game developer could experience.[/p][p][/p][p]Also, the CCC menu is available from the Grail building - which your townsfolk build for you as a reward for 'saving' them from the evils of the world. Which is a nice easter egg for Heroes of Might and Magic series.[/p][h1]Creating a Custom Class[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/83c49bdbcf28bf28aa6d4b905203610b815d2229.png"][/img][/p][p]You walk towards the majestic statue of a proud warrior your people built in the town to celebrate your victories over the evils of the world.[/p][p]You contemplate on what Adventurer you want to join your party next.[/p][p]You pick a Base Class - which governs this Class's Base HP/Energy, HP/Energy Per Level (very important!). The Class Skill of this Class will be trainable up to Grandmaster, and it doesn't cost any points.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/35cd34c6daa65bdfcbcd3e16438171cd560a87c5.png"][/img][/p][p]You spend significant time thinking what Skills you want this new Adventurer to have, and to what extent they will be trainable. It's the most important step, so you are very careful here.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/ab922b1d471f47c5b2f14c635139cf218cee3031.png"][/img][/p][p]You finalize your decisions and give the new Class a Name, a Description, and an Insignia - a visual representation of this new type of Adventurers who will kill things for you. [/p][p]You seal the deal, and are now able to create new Characters using this new Custom Class.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/9bc77084d786391e99bf6e91c5faa4127718336a.png"][/img][/p][p]You are happy. Monsters await killing in exciting new ways, you know. [/p][p][/p][h1]The game is now feature complete[/h1][p]CCC implementation concludes the list of big features we planned for the initial release. There will be QoL additions and polishing for sure, but no more significant stuff. The game is ready feature-wise.[/p][p][/p][p]The biggest remaining chunk of work for us is finalizing the content - [b]Spells, Enemies, and Maps[/b].[/p][p][/p][h1]Planned release window[/h1][p]We're aiming for the full release this Autumn.[/p][p] [/p][p]Thank you,[/p][p]13 out, went crafting my next wild party of custom-classed characters[/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Steam Next Fest Demo Update
notes.notes: [p]Hey,[/p][p][/p][p]Alex 13 here. We're participating in the Steam Next Fest, so here's the new build.[/p][p]The game is in quite a good state already, so we've focused on performance, QoL, and balance. [b]But new content is here as well![/b][/p][p][/p][h1]What's new[/h1][h2]Content[/h2][h3]Classes[/h3][p]4 new classes with their respective Class Abilities:[/p][list][*][p]Arcanist - that's a Sorc, with something like Magic Missiles, a Mana Shield, and TONS of spell damage;[/p][/*][*][p]Death Knight - inspired by a particular hero from the Warcraft universe, this is a two-handed weapons-focused tank with a casting capabilities of a dark kind. Can freeze enemies; [/p][/*][*][p]Heretic - a hybrid warrior/caster focused on Curses and utilizing this debuff to deal significant damage. Does AOE on higher levels;[/p][/*][*][p]Bard - a jack of all trades. Can, to some extent, heal, buff, debuff; deal melee, ranged, and spell damage. Sings his or her songs. It's a Bard, after all. Abilities are a song to buff and a song to debuff.[/p][/*][/list][p]Currently there are 12 Classes available in the Demo, of 35 in the full game.[/p][h3]Races[/h3][p]4 new races:[/p][list][*][p]Freeman - inspired by one of the main LOTR characters that live long enough to get good at kicking ass;[/p][/*][*][p]Dark Elf - your typical cruel pointy-ears-guys. Loves dark magic, assassinations, and making others suffer;[/p][/*][*][p]Gnome - DND fans will feel right at home with this one, as well. Those lil guys make good wizards;[/p][/*][*][p]Goblin - quite a gimmick race that will have a class custom-tailored for them in the full game. For now they are just a squishy green-skinned bois.[/p][/*][/list][h3]New Difficulty Level with some surprises[/h3][p]We've unlocked the Champion Difficulty and raised the Demo Level Cap from 12 t0 15. This is the first time you'll be able to get surprised by mobs getting new abilities as they level up. No more spoilers.[/p][p]Some buildings can now be upgraded further. [/p][h3]A new enemy[/h3][p]He's Da Boss (a mini-boss actually).[/p][h3]New warrior archetype skills[/h3][p]All warrior-meta classes now know Taunt, Block, and Parry Abilities. So they now have a bit more buttons to press :)[/p][p][/p][h2]QoL and other stuff[/h2][list][*][p]Expect +5 average FPS due to some dark under the hood magery;[/p][/*][*][p]Better damage indicators;[/p][/*][*][p]Better explanation for the Skills and Mastery systems;[/p][/*][*][p]Some balance touches here and there;[/p][/*][*][p]Arena on Town Streets map is now chance-based and not an 'every time I suffer' event;[/p][/*][*][p]This Arena is now a bit easier overall;[/p][/*][*][p][b]Item icons changed from AI-generated to what our artist created;[/b][/p][/*][*][p] Updated the in-game Roadmap;[/p][/*][*][p]Changed all tooltips from the default UE graphics to our own background images. They look better now;[/p][/*][*][p]Some Level Design/Art improvements here and there;[/p][/*][*][p]Alphabetically sorted the classes available for each race in the Character Creation scree;[/p][/*][*][p]All new characters now know their respective Beginner Class Abilities, no need to buy them;[/p][/*][*][p][b]Improved the item tooltips behavior in the Inventory screen, moved Item Comparison to Hold Left Shift;[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Improved the Hit Percentages indicator behavior;[/p][/*][*][p]Tweaked melee attack ranges for mobs and player characters;[/p][/*][*][p]Movement will now disable cursor mode;[/p][/*][/list][h3]Fixes[/h3][list][*][p]Fixed “!“ above tavern when all rewards claimed;[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed AoE damage indicator triggering on not damage events;[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed UObject limit crash in town widgets;[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed character autoswitch sometimes not working;[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed item tooltips intersecting item button;[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed some issues with Graphics settings;[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed “Apprentice” prefix permanently reducing item required level;[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed “of revenge“ suffix not doing anything.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]Save compatibility[/h1][p]Nothing critical - you can continue playing your old save. But it's still [b]recommended[/b] to start fresh. [/p][p]To do this, go to Options -> Misc -> Delete Save.[/p][p][/p][p]Have fun playing the game! [/p][p][/p][p]Thanks,[/p][p]13, DDG team and our pets. [/p][p][/p][p]13, out.[/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Announcing Titans of the Past x Trophy Hunt Collab
notes.notes:
Hey,

Alex 13 here.

We're happy to announce that we're doing a collab with another Ukrainian team, amazing guys at [url=https://trophyhunt.me/]Trophy Hunt[/url].

[h1]Giveaway[/h1]
[list]
[*] We're giving away Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. 
[*] Winner picks a platform! 
[*] Wishlist Titans of the Past and [url=https://bit.ly/45t9VX6]join the Trophy Hunt waitlist[/url] to get a chance to win this gorgeous game!
[/list]

Winner will be announced on June 9 using a raffle🍀

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/77927d086a3849895d712ab5da09e79941cf5564.png[/img]

[h1]What is Trophy Hunt?[/h1]
At [url=https://bit.ly/45t9VX6]TrophyHun[/url]t, we believe your gaming story deserves more than just a username. It’s about the time you’ve put in, the achievements you’ve earned, and the games you’ve conquered. That’s why we built a platform that brings all of it together—across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam.

Whether you’re a completionist, an achievement hunter, or someone who just enjoys playing through new worlds, TrophyHunt keeps track of everything you’ve done. It gives you a complete gaming profile that reflects who you are as a player—not just what you play, but how you play it.

[h1]Why It Matters?[/h1]
Traditional social platforms don’t capture your gaming identity. You can post clips or screenshots, but they don’t tell the full story—how many games you’ve finished, the rare trophies you’ve earned, or how far you’ve come.

TrophyHunt changes that. It’s a home for your progress, a place where your gaming life is front and center. All your stats, all your achievements, all in one profile you control and can share.
So instead of just saying you're a gamer, you can actually show it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/f3d844cbeb9b76c21198c63dd7d39f42860c4f92.png[/img]

[h1]What to expect?[/h1]
🎯 [b]One Profile for All Your Games[/b]
Connect your PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam accounts and keep all your progress in one place.
🧠 [b]Your In-Game Co-Pilot[/b]
Stuck on a boss fight or chasing 100% completion? TrophyHunt helps you figure out what’s next and how to get there—no digging through forums.
📊 [b]Leaderboards That Count[/b]
See where you stand in global rankings or within your favorite titles. Compete with friends or climb solo.
🚀 [b]Level Up and Unlock Style[/b]
Earn XP for everything you do and unlock avatars, profile frames, and rewards to personalize your space.
👥 [b]Bring Everyone Together[/b]
Find players for co-op sessions, join game discussions, and connect with your community—even if they’re on different platforms.
🎮 [b]Discover Games Through Progress[/b]
Explore what others are playing and completing. Let real achievement data guide your next pick.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/5e86636f71aebf87d887e0123df60e7898495316.png[/img]

[h1]Why gamers love it?[/h1]
Because it makes everything you’ve done in games feel meaningful. You don’t just scroll—you track progress, earn rewards, and share moments that actually matter to you.

TrophyHunt removes the friction of bouncing between platforms and gives you a space to connect with people who play the way you do. Whether you’re grinding for rare trophies or casually exploring new releases, it’s built to support your journey from start to finish.

[h1]Who it’s for?[/h1]
TrophyHunt is for anyone who plays games. You might be into 100% completions, casual weekend sessions, co-op with friends, or just looking for something new to play. It’s a space to track your progress, find like-minded players, and be part of a gaming community that actually gets you.

notes.title: Demo coming in...
notes.notes:
... May. The [b]Demo [/b]for Titans of the Past is coming [b]this May[/b]. Stay tuned - we'll announce the exact date in the coming weeks. 

Meanwhile, we've finalized a few important things. The most important of which is that Town is now completely done - all art and mechanics are in. And oh boy there are lots of mechanics: 
- Town Halls improve your gold income from adventuring
- Goblin Scout helps you find the exact loot you need
- Guild allow Mastery training and acquiring hew skills, abilities, and spells
- There are stores to trade
- The Enchanter crafts you BIS gear - if you've resources to pay for it
- There are rewards for each level of Adventure you complete - check the Tavern. And it's for each character individually!
- Buildings unlock character Races and Classes - so the more you progress the more options you have. And some combinations are straight more powerful. Lookin' at you, High Elf Necromancer
- There's a Fountain that allows you to respec

I even probably forgot something - there are lots of things going in your Town.

There are lots of things to put into the changelog, but I won't do it this time. Here's the screenshot of a Town instead.

notes.title: Development update #7
notes.notes:
Hi, Alex 13 here, with a regular update.

In a party-based RPG where fun comes from the mechanical depth, Classes have to stand out and differ. ToP's Classes already provide their rosters of skills and stat bonuses. In the future, we'll be adding 4 spell-like Abilities per Class. But for now, we've focused on adding meaningful Class Skills to further their differentiation.

Besides 33 existing Skills, we've added 35 new ones - one per Class.  Many of them are pure stat bonuses, but we also have more intricate stuff.

A few examples:
[list]
[*] Bard's Aura that gives a bonus to Attack to all party members.
[*] Sage's Aura that gives a bonus to all Resistances to all party members.
[*] Shaman's Triggered Cast of Lightning Bolt on Melee Attack.
[*] A Heretic is a high-risk / high-reward Class - they can Curse both allies and enemies with any action.
[*] Druid gives stat bonuses to Summons.
[*] Twilight Cleric gets alternating bonuses to Spell Damage and Spell Healing after casting a Healing and Damage spell, correspondingly.
[*] Goblin Magus (yes, only Goblins can get this Class) have free cast options but can miscast a spell - and hit their own party with, for example, a Fireball.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/70adc6162ce8c823a39e9bd16054f2f04c76ed94.png[/img]

Other stuff from this Sprint:
[list]
[*] A few new spells.
[*] New map finalized - Monastery.
[*] All Item bases have been created.
[*] Firearms weapon type added.
[*] Mage Weapons weapon type is now Ranged and makes pew-pew with magical energy.
[*] Added Resource pickable objects to speed your Town development.
[/list]

Thanks for reading.

notes.title: The game's new name
notes.notes:
Hi, 

Alex '13' here. Project MMl always has been a working title. It stands for Might and Magic-like, but we obviously can't keep this name. So, after thorough consideration and intense discussions within the team, the game is now called [b]Titans of the Past[/b].

[h1]The decision process[/h1]
In our team, product and design decisions are made by me and Eugene - our GD/LD, and co-founder. However, the basis for major decisions is almost always coming from the team. We always ask, then evaluate, then decide. This time was no different. I created a spreadsheet where the team could put proposals, and we gathered a nice batch of possible names this way. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/9c007cb9c05daffe6c0367223af8bf84ef0d049a.png[/img]

Then I created a poll in our Discord to vote. The idea wasn't to decide the name democratically - I don't believe in democracy in game development: from my XP, it's always better to have a final authority and responsibility within one person per area (design, code, marketing, etc.). But the voting results gave Eugene and me a perspective. 

Here are the voting results:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/d682594f4c2bb678500c63a0df8a2ecce24a6706.png[/img]
Two names stood out, and were actually good:
Echoes of Adventures and Eat. Sleep. Adventure. Repeat!
The former was going to be our new name but is already used. The latter is great, but for a different type of game - it fits a silly and slipstick-humor one, like Goat Simulator, for example. So it was obvious we shouldn't use it for Project MML, which is a tough and complex, serious fantasy RPG.

This left us with Titans of the Past. We removed the suffix (Revival) to not overcomplicate the readability. 

This name has two important meanings:
1. The pillars, core design, and feel of this game stand on the shoulders of the Titans of the Past themselves: games like Might and Magic, Wizardry, The Bard's Tale, and Eye of the Beholder. We pay our homage to the Grand Masters of the genre this way. 
2. It supports our lore and fantasy - a thing which you, the players, will be able to uncover an experience once we release the game. 

Please let me know what do you think about the game's new name.

13, out.

notes.title: Development Update #2
Development update #1
notes.notes:
Hello!

Alex '13' Uslavtsev here. Like most people in small indie teams, I do many different jobs. But mostly, I'm a producer and game designer.  Nice to meet you, dear reader. 

Today I'm here to show you our recent progress. 

As my Combat Information Cent... mmhm, excuse me, my internal progress tracker shows me - we've just passed a 40% game completion milestone. If nothing critical happens (all 7 of us are from Ukraine), we're going steadily toward the timely release. 

Recently, we updated the HUD so it looks... better. 
Before:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/4071473599ce972eb3e40419315197b7b8d382d1.jpg[/img]

After:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/a087d5d222a0df1788ee2c44d80b89981abfc3f3.png[/img]

Also, we heavily tweaked the main post-process. We tried to use it so we don't look like most of the other games (which are generally quite good games) that use the same asset packs we use. However the result didn't look good, so we removed the posterization and tweaked the color palette. Current visuals are as seen below:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45101965/3196969210948f86967d6ccf2938b19feeb34257.png[/img]

On the code front, the Adventure Generation is 2 weeks from finalization - which, for such a big feature, is almost done. We already have:
- the node graph generation
- store functionality (so you can buy this-adventure-only upgrades and resources for your Town)
- all planned Boons
- mobs spawn randomization
- all types of nodes working properly
- 7 of the planned 10 Dungeon Modifiers 

The next steps are to implement the remaining 3 Damage Mods, then do the Mob Mods, then set everything up - and we're good. 

This will conclude our current milestone. I will probably do another post once the milestone is done. 

Ah, last but not least: we've updated this Steam page with new screenshots and a new trailer, which is also below:

[previewyoutube=8mr8lNTEtfc;full][/previewyoutube]

That's all for today. 
Thank you for your attention. 13, out.
